mainText: This is Dose of Good for Thursday, November 12. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Scientists describe two new howler monkey species in the Brazilian Amazon. Using over 2 terabytes of genetic data, researchers named Alouatta matogrossensis in the southern Amazon and Alouatta iroi in the northwest. In Alta Floresta, a canopy bridge is already used by mothers with babies. Second: A 1.5 km coral colony is thriving off a remote Australian island. Over 12 dives, researchers mapped a 1.56 km rose coral colony off the Cocos Islands, one of the largest ever recorded. Deep reefs like this may shelter corals hit by bleaching. Third: Quick field test could help save Tasmanian devils from contagious cancer. University of Tasmania researchers built a portable mouth-swab test that detects the disease in the field instead of waiting days for lab results. Fourth: Exercising before therapy helps the brain in depression. In a trial involving a University of São Paulo researcher, 12 weeks of exercise before CBT improved fitness and memory and learning gains during therapy. Fifth: Brazil's Light for All programme turns 23, having powered 3.8 million families. Since 2023 about 950,000 people have gained electricity, 400,000 of them in remote parts of the Amazon. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
